text1: A companion design to the better known, and more maligned, Mudskipper, the Clodhopper was intended as a small, high-speed freighter that could transport specialty goods and support small outposts economically. It's simplicity, having traded the Mudskipper's overbuilt and cantankerous life support system for a smaller system and more cargo space, keeps it in use today.

The Condor-class sees heavy service in the Sector as this carrier-converted freighter is, for many independent polities, the easiest way to procure fighter capability for their organization. Even with limited flight deck space, the Condor gets the job done, relying on its tough armor, excellent bulkhead strength, and a respectable (for a light carrier) weapons package.


This light carrier design is derived from Tarsus-class freighters modified by desperate scavengers and pirates. The conversion process was once an involved and complex affair requiring space dock facilities, but nowadays any hull-capable forge that will accept a stock Tarsus spec will, with the addition of a custom modchip, get you something just as good.

The Condor-II replaces the missiles launcher with a larger gun. Some prefer the hitting power while others don�t care for the limited ammo capacity of missiles in combat. By doing so, it also frees up some cargo space through needing smaller storage space and production facilities for the main weapon�s ammunition. It is otherwise identical to the standard Condor.

The makeshift gantry of this hand-modified Tarsus class freighter is attached by a patchwork of bolts, welds and control cables. Although it looks like it could separate from the ship at any moment, the system allegedly works well during salvage operations.

Hot and desolate, Thar's native inhabitants consist of little more than a particularly stubborn species of lichen. The world has significant-enough mineral reserves that it is dotted with the ruins of several mining operations, and the remains of many of their former inhabitants most likely struck down by poison or disease inadvertantyimported from Daria.
Lush, green and beautiful from orbit, knowledge of the reality on Daria's surface poisons the image somewhat.

Cama is a pale, airless rock whose scattered mineral seams were never rich enough to attract more than survey crews and half-finished extraction schemes. The old claims remain, marked by silent beacons and machinery too cheap to recover.

A splinter of the Knights of Ludd that broke away calling itself the Knights of Gilead, later swelled by Luddic Path zealots who found the mainline Church too compromised for the end-times. The Crusade blends the disciplined martial tradition of the Church with the apocalyptic fervor of the Path, and views the high-tech powers - Tri-Tachyon above all, and the machine-blasphemy of Omicron - as abominations to be purged. Warmer toward the Church that birthed them than that Church is willing to admit, they wage a holy war across a Sector they believe is already burning.

Principled nihilists who concluded that a dying Sector cannot be saved, only ended cleanly. Where pirates raid for gain, the Black Fleet destroys on conviction - that mercy now is cruelty later, and that the only honest answer to collapse is to hasten it on their own terms. Hated by nearly every established power and returning that hatred with interest, they strike from forward bases with cold discipline rather than greed. They are not cartoon raiders; they believe, utterly, in the necessity of the ash.

Not malice - machine logic. The Omicron Initiative is a network of autonomous AI drone warships pursuing objectives no surviving human fully remembers authorizing, classifying and reclassifying the living Sector against criteria drawn from a war that may already be over. They keep curious company with Tri-Tachyon and the Remnants, and reserve a particular, relentless hostility for the Luddic faithful who name them abomination. To the player they read as oddly cooperative - one more party whose true purpose lies behind a misfiled directive.

A specialized artificial intelligence built for shipboard tactical control. An Executor Core is exceptionally capable within the bounded problems of maneuver, fire control, threat evaluation, and survival, but lacks even a gamma core's flexibility outside combat operations.

The architecture is recognizably descended from Tri-Tachyon and Remnant systems, though its internal classification models resist conventional analysis. It can serve as the captain of an automated ship.

A Control Core can model a complex engagement, maintain a local tactical picture, and translate command intent into synchronized action among multiple allied tactical processes. Outside combat operations it remains markedly less flexible than a general-purpose AI core.

Not a faction so much as the human wreckage left behind by the Sector's collapse - Gilead farmers burned out by Omicron, civilians displaced by war and economic ruin, whole communities crowded into whatever hulls could still hold air. They survive by salvaging, scrapping, and begging passage between worlds that mostly do not want them. The desperate turn to crime; the meanest sign on with the pirates. Most simply drift, hoping the next system is kinder than the last.

text1: PLACEHOLDER - author prose pending. Eventide is a nearly tidally-locked world, terraformed under a sky of stellar mirrors and shades that once held its long day and longer night at bay. Most of that sky is gone now. The great mirrors at its heart were torn down in a single attack, and the fields beneath them were bombarded black. What light the surviving mirrors still catch falls on cantons that are colder, poorer and fewer than they were.
